chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sha'iri, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
There are two classes of my Nation which, if they are rectified, my Nation is rectified, and if they are corrupted, my Nation is corrupted: the rulers and the reciters.

key_terms.الأمراء: Rulers, commanders, governors — those holding political authority
key_terms.القراء: Reciters, scholars of the Quran — the religious and intellectual leadership of the community
key_terms.صلح: To be righteous, rectified, good — the opposite of corruption
key_terms.صنفان: Two classes/types — a dual noun indicating precisely two categories

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the two classes that determine the fate of the Muslim community?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warns that the moral and spiritual condition of the Muslim community depends critically on two pivotal groups: the rulers (umara') who hold political authority, and the reciters/scholars (qurra') who are the custodians of religious knowledge. This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his forebears, emphasizes the outsized responsibility borne by those in positions of leadership and learning. In the early Islamic context, 'qurra'' referred not merely to those who recite the Quran but to those learned in religion who served as moral guides; their rectitude or corruption sets the tone for the entire community.
